data.name: Horil
data.gender_notes: Horil is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Horil is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Horas' which means radiant light. This name is associated with the goddess Horsha, symbolizing illumination, wisdom, and inner strength. It is believed that a child named Horil will bring light and knowledge to those around them. The name Horil carries the meaning “Radiant Light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Horil usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant light and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Horil was a mythological figure in Hinduism, mentioned in various Puranas as a great warrior and an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. He is described as having slain the demon Virochana and liberated the gods from his tyranny.

Horil is also mentioned in the Mahabharata epic as the father of Bhishma, who was the grandsire of the Pandava and Kaurava dynasties. Bhishma is renowned for his vow of lying on a bed of arrows, and his role in the great Kurukshetra war.
